Title: Two agents choosing the same seat at the same time
Notes: EXCLUDED - removed from scope by human decision (Mohanad Dawood, 2026-09-27): not to be executed; commented out in the test sheet. Was Not Executed. Opening a second tab in the SAME browser redirected to a 'Multiple Tabs Detected' / 'Session Protection Enabled' screen. Inspecting localStorage showed this guard keys off a 'sessionId' value stored in localStorage, which is scoped per browser profile and is never shared across two genuinely different browsers (or two different profiles/incognito windows) - confirmed with the human operator. So this guard only catches an accidental duplicate tab in one browser; it would NOT stop two different browsers (or two different agents) from reaching the same seat map concurrently, and the case's real scenario (a genuine two-agent race for one seat) remains unproven either way. This pass's tooling controls a single browser instance with no way to launch a second, independent browser/profile, so the precondition could not be constructed. Recorded as Not Executed (a tooling limitation this session), not as evidence the app is safe or unsafe here.

Title: A child CANNOT take an exit seat
Notes: REVISED 2026-09-27: initially logged Failed, believing the Portal's PNR-wide exit-row block was a defect. The human operator then checked the LIVE flynas.com production site directly (booking.flynas.com) with a 3-pax booking (Ahmad Ismail with Infant, Ahmad Mahmoud, Rawan Ahmad) and confirmed rows 11 and 12 (exit rows) show 'X - Restricted' for every seat, for every passenger card selected - including the two adults with NO infant linked to them. The Portal's behaviour exactly matches the real airline's production system. This is not an app defect: the case's own expected result ('the adult still can') is the part that is incorrect - the real business rule is PNR-wide, not per-passenger. Reclassified from Failed to Passed (app behaves correctly); the case's written expectation needs revision, not the app.

Title: The rule is rechecked when you switch passenger
Notes: REVISED 2026-09-27 - see TC-SM-EXR-003 for the full reasoning. The case's premise (the seat starts bookable for at least the qualifying adult, then flips when the child is selected) does not hold in the real airline's system either: flynas.com itself shows the exit row as 'X - Restricted' for every passenger from the outset, confirmed via 3 screenshots (one per passenger card) on the live production site with only 1 infant in the party. The Portal correctly reproduces this. Reclassified from Failed to Passed.

Title: The rule follows the infant's linked adult
Notes: REVISED 2026-09-27 - see TC-SM-EXR-003 for the full reasoning. The case expects the refusal to be exclusive to whichever adult the infant is linked to, and to MOVE when re-linked. Confirmed against the live flynas.com production site that the real rule is PNR-wide (any infant in the party blocks the whole exit row for everyone), not link-specific - so there is no 'exclusive to A, moves to B' behaviour to reproduce in the first place. The Portal's static, PNR-wide block matches the real airline exactly. Reclassified from Failed to Passed; the case's premise about a movable, link-specific refusal is incorrect.
